title: Failure of quadratic restriction produces a cohomological subcluster obstruction
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume $C$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes with completed local rings $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $h^i(C,F)=\dim_k H^i(C,F)$ for Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Assume that $L$ has a global section nonzero at the generic point of every irreducible component. Let $S\subset C$ be a finite reduced closed subscheme supported in the smooth locus, possibly empty. For a closed subscheme $T\subseteq S$, write $I_T$ for its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and use module pullback for restriction [def-pc-module-pullback]. If the map
$$H^0(C,L)\otimes_k H^0(C,L)\longrightarrow H^0(S,(L^{\otimes2})|_S),\qquad a\otimes b\longmapsto (ab)|_S,$$
with the tensor-section multiplication of [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], is not surjective, there exists a nonempty closed subscheme $T\subseteq S$ such that
$$h^0(C,I_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}L)+h^1(C,I_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}L)\geq h^0(C,L)+h^1(C,L).$$
Tensor products use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: The projective curve $C$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [def-sc-invertible-module], $L$ is quasi-coherent and locally generated by one element, so [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes it coherent. Proper coherent cohomology [lem-pc-coherent-hi] makes $H^0(C,L)$ and $H^1(C,L)$ finite-dimensional. Put $V=H^0(C,L)$.

proof.text: Because $S$ is finite over $k$, it is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a finite-dimensional commutative $k$-algebra $A$. It is Artinian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] and reduced by the hypothesis on $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] to obtain $A\cong\prod_x A/\mathfrak m_x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields], $S$ is the finite disjoint union of the open singleton schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m_x)$. Since $S$ is finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] identifies every factor with $k$. Choose a basis $e_x$ of each line $L|_x$ using [def-sc-invertible-module]. Sheaf gluing on these disjoint opens identifies $H^0(S,L|_S)=k^{|S|}$ and identifies $H^0(S,L^{\otimes2}|_S)$ with the same coordinate space using $e_x^{\otimes2}$. Under these choices a restricted product has coordinates $a(x)b(x)$ by [def-sc-invertible-section-ring].

proof.text: On $k^T$ define $B(z,w)=\sum_{x\in T}c_xz_xw_x$. This is bilinear and nondegenerate: testing against each coordinate vector gives $c_xz_x=0$, hence $z_x=0$, and the identical calculation works in the other argument. The preceding annihilation equation says $B(W,W)=0$, so $W\subseteq W^\perp$. By [lem-sfb-nondegenerate-orthogonal-dimension], $\dim W^\perp=n-\dim W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity] to the injective inclusion $W\hookrightarrow W^\perp$: its kernel is zero, so $r:=\dim W\le n-r$. Consequently $2r\le n$. This uses bilinearity, with no division by $2$ and no restriction on the characteristic.

proof.text: Write $i:T\hookrightarrow C$, $F=I_T\otimes L$ and $Q=i_*(L|_T)$. The defining ideal sequence [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is short exact: on an affine chart it is $0\to I\to A\to A/I\to0$. Tensor with $L$ by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. Its quotient is $Q$: on an open trivializing $L$, the quotient is $\mathcal O_C/I_T=i_*\mathcal O_T$; the gluing maps on both sides multiply by the restriction of the same transition unit of $L$. This gives $0\to F\to L\to Q\to0$. Since $T$ is a finite disjoint union of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, it is Noetherian of dimension zero, and $L|_T$ is quasi-coherent. Thus [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^1(T,L|_T)=0$. Apply [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] on both $C$ and $T$, and [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] to the underlying abelian sheaf on $T$: this proves $H^1(C,Q)=0$. Also $H^0(C,Q)=H^0(T,L|_T)=k^T$ directly from the definition of direct image.

proof.text: The category of $\mathcal O_C$-modules has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], and global sections are additive and left exact by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to the preceding sequence, with module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Its initial part is $0\to H^0(C,F)\to V\to k^T\to H^1(C,F)\to H^1(C,L)\to0$. Write $a=h^0(C,L)$ and $b=h^1(C,L)$. Exactness gives two short exact sequences of vector spaces, $0\to H^0(C,F)\to V\to W\to0$ and $0\to k^T/W\to H^1(C,F)\to H^1(C,L)\to0$. By rank-nullity [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity] (equivalently choose lifts of a basis of a quotient) all spaces here are finite-dimensional and $h^0(C,F)=a-r$, $h^1(C,F)=n-r+b$. Therefore $h^0(C,F)+h^1(C,F)=a+b+n-2r\ge a+b$, by Step 4. The nonempty $T\subseteq S$ constructed in Step 3 proves the assertion.
